Synthesis: agents move from reactive single-turn assistants to proactive, multi-turn, tool-augmented agents; benchmarks mostly Python, small, self-contained and non-interactive (SWE-Bench 65% function-level); toolchains and languages are human-centric; memory, safety, multi-agent protocols and domain adaptation remain open

Gaps in the field: benchmarks for real workflows (multi-language, large code bases, interactive and tool-integrated tasks); metrics beyond functional correctness; standard multi-agent protocols; domain-specific models; safety, privacy and trust; toolchains exposing structured feedback and IR; scalable memory; human-AI collaboration; structured languages to state intent and constraints. Limitations of the survey itself: not discussed

Search period and cut-off date not stated (web sources accessed 2025-09-15). Fig. 6 legend shows Boolean OR between the term clusters, the text says 'Boolean operators' (pp. 11-12).
